config.title: Unnecessary Re-renders

intro.title: Unnecessary Re-renders
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application with a counter and a text input to observe how components re-render. You will learn the concept of unnecessary re-renders, which occur when a component updates its UI even when its data hasn't changed, potentially slowing down your app. The main technologies involved are React functional components, the useState hook for state management, and TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll understand how to identify and prevent these re-renders to optimize your React applications.
intro.usecase: Unnecessary re-renders frequently impact performance in data-intensive applications like financial dashboards or e-commerce product filters. When users interact with complex filtering controls or live-updating metrics panels, poorly optimized components can cause sluggish UI responses. Developers encounter this when building interactive data tables where sorting one column shouldn't re-render unrelated visualization widgets. Mastering re-render prevention ensures smooth user experiences in real-time applications like collaborative editing tools or live sports score trackers.

objectives: Implement React.memo to prevent unnecessary re-renders of functional components
Apply useMemo to memoize expensive calculations and optimize performance
Construct a custom comparison function for React.memo to control re-render behavior
Configure useCallback to memoize event handlers and prevent unnecessary re-creations
Update component props and state while identifying unnecessary re-render triggers
Integrate React DevTools Profiler to analyze and measure component re-renders
Manipulate dependency arrays in useMemo and useCallback to optimize re-render conditions

steps.title: Initialize state for counter and toggle
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use useState to declare two state variables: count (a number) and isActive (a boolean). Initialize count to 0 and isActive to false.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook twice: once for count and once for isActive. Remember to provide the correct initial values and TypeScript will infer the types.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables ready to trigger re-renders when updated.
successCriteria: The component contains two useState calls: one for count (initialized to 0) and one for isActive (initialized to false).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both state variables: count (number) and isActive (boolean) with the correct initial values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using useState inside the component to declare both state variables with proper initial values.

steps.title: Define a regular handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, define a function named incrementCount that increments the count state by 1.
steps.hint: Use the setCount function from useState to update the state. The function should take no parameters and call setCount with the current count plus 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: The incrementCount function is defined and will cause unnecessary re-renders when used later.
successCriteria: The incrementCount function is defined inside the App component and calls setCount to increment the count state by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named incrementCount and properly increments the count state by calling setCount.
steps.feedbackWrong: The incrementCount function is not defined correctly. It should be inside the App component and update the count state by 1.

steps.title: Define a memoized handler with useCallback
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a memoized function called toggleActive using useCallback that toggles the isActive state value.
steps.hint: Use the useCallback hook with an empty dependency array to memoize the function so it doesn't recreate on every render.
steps.expectedOutcome: A memoized toggleActive function that toggles the isActive state when called.
successCriteria: The toggleActive function is defined with useCallback, has an empty dependency array, and toggles the isActive state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using useCallback with an empty dependency array and properly toggling the isActive state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleActive function should be defined with useCallback and toggle the isActive state value. Try using setIsActive with a function that returns the opposite of the current state.
